descriptor: Day-boat seafood restaurant cooked over fire

voice.summary: Brine & Co talks like a harbour kitchen: short, sensory and a bit cheeky. It names the boat, the port and the pan, then lets the food do the persuading.
dos: Name the catch and the port before any adjective
Use cooking verbs: char, crisp, shuck, flash-fry
Keep menu descriptions to one line
donts: Do not call anything gourmet, artisan or fusion
Never pretend the catch is the same every day

taglines: Fresh off the boat, onto the plate
Caught at dawn, cooked by dinner
Simple fish, hot pan, open fire
boilerplate: Brine & Co is a seafood restaurant serving day-boat catch from Pittenweem, cooked simply over fire or in a hot pan, with a menu that changes with the tide.

microcopy.success: Table booked. We will keep the oysters cold.
microcopy.error: That did not go through. Try again, or ring us.
microcopy.empty: Nothing in this section today. The boats are still out.

logo.note: A flame points to cooking over fire and sits well against the harbour teal and crab orange.
